newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Customs crackdown on imported cars clogs NZ port.
newsitem.headline: Customs crackdown on imported cars clogs NZ port.

text.p: Thousands of Japanese used cars clogged Auckland's commercial docks on Thursday while customs officials inspected them for tampered odometers.

The traffic jam at New Zealand's busiest port got so bad that port authorities permitted the car carrier "Palma" to unload just 400 of its 1,100-car cargo. The remainder will be offloaded at Wellington and Christchurch harbours. Port spokeswoman Karen Beanland said Queens, Marsden and Captain Cook wharves were all at capacity.
Customs officials swooped on the docks at the weekend after widespread reports that importers had been evading tax by undervaluing cars and also winding back odometers to make the cars appear newer.
The Customs Department estimates that importers have evaded paying tax of about NZ$100 million (US$68.9 million) by undervaluing cars.
New Zealanders have flocked to buy Japanese used cars, which quickly become obsolete in their home country because of highly stringent roadworthiness laws there.
The imports have raised the ire of the major international car makers, who have seen their New Zealand profits eroded by the relatively cheap used car alternative.
